title: av_extend_guts after an unshift leaves the trailing element slots holding stale SV pointers
live_proof: upstream fixed it in 9e298ab597 (9e298ab597b2c6fc0741749d7e29119e2d6cd628) (2023-07-18). That commit is an ancestor of v5.45.3-85-gdb19522155 and is NOT an ancestor of the v5.36.3 tag (checked with git merge-base --is-ancestor, both directions), so it never reached the 5.36 maintenance branch; the pin's tree shows the unfixed code (pin av.c:111 to_null = *arrayp - *allocp; av.c:118 newmax = key + *maxp; goto resize with no to_null correction). Host ASan at the pin: ASan: SEGV (rc=77); the same trigger, same harness and same ASan options on master: no report (rc=0, the harness reports [PASS])
fidelity: the trigger is the test upstream added with its own fix, extracted onto a self-contained harness that collects failures instead of aborting, so one script yields one verdict. It is upstream's own reproduction, not a reduction of ours; what it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it

sysalloc-bounds.oracle: no fault: completes and the workload's own oracle passes

sysalloc-sublet.oracle: no fault: completes and the workload's own oracle passes

sublet-svheads.oracle: no fault: completes and the workload's own oracle passes

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: no report: completes; with revocation off (_RUNTIME_REVOCATION_DISABLE=1) the same binary gives: no report: completes

status: all three Capstone arms measured 2026-10-06 on the Capstone application VM, each after passing its own two controls; cheribsd-revocation measured 2026-10-06 on CheriBSD purecap, revocation selected per process because the system-wide default kills the guest's sshd, and every case run under both settings so the pair controls the knob (results/20261006-cheribsd)
allocator_layer: system allocator (the AV element array, via Renew)
note: not triggered by this trigger anywhere but the host: its own assertion PASSES on all four Capstone arms AND on CheriBSD with revocation both off and on, so the stale element slot the defect depends on never holds a stale pointer there. Its silence is not evidence about any arm and it is outside every denominator. Host ASan at the pin reports SEGV, so the defect is real; what is missing is a trigger that reproduces it under an allocator other than glibc
